findings.rootCause: PackedFilterRules.apply, freely-relocatable branch: `leftContains = maskContainsAll(relOutputMaskId(left), deps)` (same for right) decided the operand from the operand's POSSIBLE output mask. A LeftJoin factor's output mask includes its optional-side variables, so under the fallback placement path (PackedIncumbentSearch.applyUncoveredFilterPlacement: lattice not completed because of a tight work budget or >DENSE_FACTOR_LIMIT=16 factors) `FILTER(?x = ?y)` was pushed onto `{ ?s :p ?y OPTIONAL { ?s :q ?x } }` although the sibling `?s :r ?x` binds ?x for every row; rows whose OPTIONAL left ?x unbound were dropped (row s=urn:t:a lost for workLimit 1..MAX with 18 extra factors). The dense lattice and the guarded-correlated branch of the same rule already used relAssuredMaskId, so only this branch was unsound; results depended on budget and query width.
findings.change: Mirrors BindingScopeAnalysis.canPushInto bit-for-bit with masks (roadmap 4.1, possible names may only block): an operand qualifies only when its output mask covers the dependencies AND (deps ∩ possible(sibling)) ⊆ assured(operand), via a new allocation-free accessor PackedQuery.maskContainsAllIntersection -> PackedBindingFacts.containsAllIntersection -> the existing PackedMaskInterner.containsAllIntersection primitive (already used by containsAllScheduledDependencies). When neither operand qualifies the rule returns 1 and the filter stays at the join. Sound because a filter's outcome depends only on its variables, each of which is either forced equal by join compatibility (assured in the operand) or cannot be changed by the sibling. Lattice placements are unaffected; positive shapes (variable assured by the LeftJoin's left arg, or absent from the sibling) still push and are pinned by tests. Primitive-only, so the PackedQueryCodecTest hot-path audit that lists PackedFilterRules stays green (20/0).

findings.rootCause: ScalarEvaluationEffects.functionEffect was an allowlist: REPEATABLE only when the Function implementation class name started with `org.eclipse.rdf4j.query.algebra.evaluation.function.` AND shared the CodeSource of Function.class; every other registered function (GeoSPARQL geof:*, SPIN, user functions) was UNKNOWN unless all its arguments were constants (then QUERY_STABLE as a workaround). combine() propagates UNKNOWN through And, so FilterOptimizer neither split `STRSTARTS(?n,..) && geof:sfWithin(?wkt,..)` nor relocated either conjunct (both pinned above the join in all stores), PackedQueryCodec did not set SCALAR_REORDERING_SAFE, and LMDB learning keys excluded such filters. auditedModelOperator/auditedTupleOperator also required CodeSource equality, so a null CodeSource (native image, some class loaders) turned every model operator UNKNOWN and disabled relocation entirely. The engine's only volatility contract, Function.mustReturnDifferentResult(), is what ConstantOptimizer and DefaultEvaluationStrategy already trust.
findings.change: Denylist per the design: functionEffect = UNKNOWN for an unregistered IRI (cannot be evaluated; fail closed), VOLATILE when mustReturnDifferentResult(), propagate VOLATILE/UNKNOWN arguments, QUERY_STABLE for Now, otherwise the arguments' effect (REPEATABLE, or QUERY_STABLE inherited from a NOW() argument). Removed auditedCoreFunction, valueArgsAreConstant, the constant-arguments->QUERY_STABLE special case and sameCodeSource. auditedModelOperator/auditedTupleOperator use exact package equality with org.eclipse.rdf4j.query.algebra (foreign subclasses such as LmdbValueVar, FedX operators and test doubles still fail closed; the ForeignUnaryValueExpr test stays UNKNOWN). Effect enum Javadoc now states the two guarantees (placement needs reorderingIsSafe; LMDB learning keys need REPEATABLE = stable across queries) and names the core/spin follow-up, addressing the critique minor. Consumers become strictly more permissive for deterministic custom functions, which is the develop baseline for placement.

findings.rootCause: Two LMDB-only defects behind SES869ValueOfNow (`SELECT ?p (NOW() AS ?n) { BIND(NOW() AS ?p) }`, asserting p == n). (a) ConstantOptimizer folds both NOW() calls into ValueConstants holding one shared literal; LmdbValueLookupOptimizer.meet(ValueConstant)/meet(Var) then called lookup(value) per node and ValueStore.getLmdbValue creates a fresh LmdbLiteral wrapper per call, so the two constants ended up distinct-but-equal (assertEquals passes, assertSame fails). (b) Critique major: the LMDB pipeline plan cache keys on the un-optimized tree and caches the fully optimized template, on which NOW() is already folded; LmdbPipelinePlanCache.ReusableInputVisitor refused only Service and non-Collection VALUES, so every cache hit replayed the first execution's timestamp (confirmed red by LmdbValueLookupIdentityTest#nowIsReevaluatedOnRepeatedExecution after the memo fix alone).
findings.change: (a) LmdbValueLookupOptimizer.Visitor keeps an IdentityHashMap<Value, Lookup> for one optimize() pass so every node holding the same Value instance resolves to the same LmdbValue wrapper (also removes redundant ValueStore round-trips); the unknown-id marker semantics (knownValue == null for values absent from the store) are unchanged and pinned by a test. (b) LmdbPipelinePlanCache.ReusableInputVisitor marks the query non-reusable when the source tree (inspected before folding) contains a FunctionCall whose ScalarEvaluationEffects effect is QUERY_STABLE, i.e. NOW(); the plan is then recomputed per request so the clock is re-read. Kept narrow: REPEATABLE and VOLATILE calls are not affected (VOLATILE calls are never folded, so a cached template is fine for them).
